text:
maria-ng: Heads up — saw a 12% p99 latency regression on Mixtral MoE serving after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. Anyone else?

eli: yup noticed it on Canary 2. Routing tail latencies spiked around 1.2s for some shards. Not constant but correlated with high top-k routing.

jonathan-k: thanks for flagging. Which change specifically? The new AVX fused attention path?

maria-ng: the change picked the 'fused_gemm_attn_v2' kernel for attention when seq_len <= 512 and batch >= 8. It reduces CPU overhead normally but I think it interacts badly with router hot paths for MoE.

eli: I profiled a few slow traces — stack shows time spent in router logits softmax + gather, not the attention kernel itself. But the kernel selection changed memory layout so KV cache hits/misses pattern changed.

sophia: interesting. Can you paste the perf snippet?

eli: sure — trimmed flame:

```
# slow trace summary
20.3% router_logits_softmax
16.7% gather_expert_indices
14.1% attention_fused_gemm_v2
11.9% kv_cache_read (remote misses)
8.4% cuda_memcpy_async
```

maria-ng: note the kv_cache_read remote misses — that's the one that jumped from ~2% to ~12% after the change. Means routing pattern caused more cross-expert cache pressure.

jonathan-k: what about top-k routing param? We recently bumped top_k from 2 -> 3 in the A/B config for better quality. Could that amplify pressure?

sophia: yes, top_k=3 increases duplicate expert touches per token, which increases contention for expert local caches and increases gather costs. Combined with the kernel mem layout change, cache line alignment might be worse.

maria-ng: quick mitigation idea: revert kernel selector for Mixtral MoE to prefer non-fused path when model_type=="mixture_of_experts" OR when top_k>2.

eli: can also try limiting expert_parallelism to reduce simultaneous hot expert threads — reduces per-GPU outstanding KV reads. For Canary we can set expert_parallelism=0.5 (i.e. half the usual parallelism) and measure.

jonathan-k: another angle: smarter batching heuristics — avoid large continuous batches of same routing hot-expert keys. We could insert jitter into batch packing to spread expert load.

sophia: agreed. Also adding a small LRU for expert indices at router level (short TTL) could filter repeated hits inside a single batch and reduce mem ops.

maria-ng: plan: 1) roll kernel selector revert for MoE on Canary-2; 2) run expert_parallelism throttling experiment; 3) revert top_k bump in A/B if needed. I'll open a PR.

jonathan-k: +1. Please add a perf-bot measurement run with these variants: baseline, kernel_revert, parallelism_0.5, topk_2. We need p50/p95/p99 + kv_cache_miss_rate.

perf-bot: perf run queued: mixtral_moe/canary-2/variants [baseline,kernel_revert,parallelism_0.5,topk_2]. ETA ~ 25m. Results will be posted here.

eli: one more note — RoPE scaling we rolled last week can slightly change attention weight distribution; that can indirectly affect routing logits magnitude and numerical stability in softmax. Might explain the softmax time increase for extreme tokens. Recommend adding a tiny entropy regularizer in router logits computation as an experiment.

sophia: good call. small damping term + temperature tweak could reduce extremely peaked distributions and spread load. Worth testing after immediate mitigations.

maria-ng: thanks team. I'll PR the kernel revert and the experiment configs now. Will post links to PR and perf results. :rocket:

perf-bot: perf run complete: kernel_revert reduced p99 by 9%, kv_cache_miss_rate down from 11.8% -> 3.0% on Canary-2. parallelism_0.5 reduced p95 by 6% but increased latency variance. Detailed logs: https://perf.internal/runs/1775067890.

eli: awesome — sounds like kernel+kv interaction was the main culprit. Let's keep top_k=3 in prod A/B for quality, but activate kernel heuristic for MoE only.

jonathan-k: agree. Follow-up tasks: add a kernel selector unit test that simulates repeated expert routing and validates kv miss delta < 1%.

maria-ng: noted. I'll file follow-ups in the ticket and assign tests. Closing the loop here once PR merges.

sophia: thanks all :thumbsup:
